chapter.heading: A Prayer of Faith in Time of DistressTo the Chief Musician. With stringed instruments. On an eight-stringed harp. A Psalm of David.
chapter.v:
O Lord,
do not rebuke me in Your anger,Nor chasten me in Your hot displeasure. [[Matt. 16:18; 1 Cor. 3:9, 10; Eph. 2:20-22; 1 Pet. 2:5]]

Have mercy
on me, O Lord, for I am weak;O Lord, heal me, for my bones are troubled. [Prov. 23:30] [Matt. 22:4]

My soul
also is greatly troubled;But You, O Lord—how long?

Return, O
Lord, deliver me!Oh, save me for Your mercies’ sake! [Ps. 19:7]

For in
death there is no remembrance of You;In the grave who will give You thanks? [Song 5:1; Is. 55:1; [John 6:27]]

I am
weary with my groaning;All night I make my bed swim;I drench my couch with my tears.

My eye
wastes away because of grief;It grows old because of all my enemies.

Depart from
me, all you workers of iniquity;For the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping. [Prov. 15:12; Matt. 7:6 g Ps. 141:5; Prov. 10:8]

The Lord
has heard my supplication;The Lord will receive my prayer. [[Matt. 13:12]]

Let all
my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled;Let them turn back and be ashamed suddenly. [Job 28:28; Ps. 111:10; Prov. 1:7]
